Yellow Face from the Suffering of People

"Feeling the Sorrow of Others" in a Tale by Saadi

In the story of the Damascus famine, Saadi speaks of a man who is not himself in financial hardship, yet the suffering of the hungry robs him of pleasure. Can one, in times of war, economic hardship, and insecurity, both worry about the suffering of others and continue living?

In this episode, inspired by Saadi's tale, we explore the meaning of empathy in difficult days; we speak about the necessity of compassion and reducing the suffering of others, and we reflect on how the flood of images of suffering on social media can gradually desensitize us. In this segment, we will also seek answers to these questions: Is happiness in times of hardship a sign of indifference, and how can discontent become a criterion for judging others?

entry.title: [sahandiranmehr] Imagination is a realm in which a person can at least be the hero of their own…
entry.summary:
Machine-translated from the original Telegram post.

Source: @sahandiranmehr

Imagination is a realm in which a person can at least be the hero of their own destiny; a world from which no power has yet managed to take away their right to claim it as their own. Let us suppose the Israelis made this video; but you who repost it with such enthusiasm and pride—why do you not want this dream to be realized by your own hands and your own people, even in your imagination? Why, even in the dream of power, must someone else seat you on the throne? Imagination, though it is a playground where we wrestle with reality, is also a reflection of a person's hidden longings. In the solitude of imagination, a person is at least themselves, or their people, the hero of their own story. A person takes joy, at the very least, in what their own mind creates—rather than having someone else create their imagination for them too! Is it not astonishing that even in your dream, the hero is someone else, and you and your people remain spectators to the will of others?✍🏻Sahand Iranmehr@sahandiranmehr

entry.title: [sahandiranmehr] Netanyahu says that in July 2025, at the same time as the clashes between…
entry.summary:
Machine-translated from the original Telegram post.

Source: @sahandiranmehr

Netanyahu says that in July 2025, at the same time as the clashes between Syrian government forces and the Druze community, he called Ahmed al-Sharaa, the president of Syria, and had a conversation that, according to him, was "very short and very sharp." Netanyahu said: "We destroyed the Ministry of Defense in Damascus, just like that; it was over and done with." Netanyahu says with pride that we struck Syria's Ministry of Defense and spoke sharply with al-Sharaa by phone. This is the naked logic of Israel in the regional order, and the countries of the region are treated not as states possessing sovereignty, but as geography whose red lines must be determined by Israel. In this logic, Israel's security is another name for the right to intervene in the security of others, and aggression takes on the language of protecting minorities—but how does a state that commits genocide become a protector of the Druze minority, and on that basis grant itself the legitimacy to strike another country's Ministry of Defense? Is the goal only the protection of a minority, or the creation of a buffer region, the de facto fragmentation of southern Syria, and the paving of the way for domination or even annexation of parts of the Druze-populated region? Without pausing, what other minorities does this logic, in its own outlook, consider within the scope of imposing its order in the region?✍🏻Sahand Iranmehr@sahandiranmehr
